meta.report_title: Customers want to smell it before they buy

snapshot.intro: Scent is both the biggest reason people buy and the biggest reason they nearly don't. Fix how scent comes across online and you move both at once.
snapshot.note: All-time runs from 1 June to 30 September 2026. Bases differ by question because not every respondent answers every question.

items.text: Add 'smells like' comparisons to every candle page
items.note: Live from 4 August. Too early for the objection share to show it; it is in line with all-time this period.

items.text: Add a breakage guarantee line to product pages and the cart
items.note: Still the top reason inside the shipping objection (13 of 23).

insights.title: A third of buyers nearly didn't buy because they couldn't smell it
insights.body: 101 of 291 new customers named it, more than price, burn time and shipping combined. The follow-up says the problem is vague descriptions (39 of 85), not the lack of samples (27 of 85).
insights.action: Rewrite scent descriptions on the top 5 candles as 'smells like' comparisons before anything else.
insights.source: Main objection question and scent follow-up, all-time

insights.title: The scent copy is also why people buy
insights.body: The scent descriptions are the top reason to buy (88 of 298). The same lever answers the top objection and feeds the top angle, so it is the highest-return piece of copy on the site.
insights.action: Lead Meta ads with a specific scent picture, not with the wax or the brand.

insights.title: Price is not the problem and does not need a discount
insights.body: 42 of 291 named price, steady this period. Of those who explained, 16 of 36 were really asking about burn hours for the money, which is a copy fix, not a price fix.
insights.action: Show cost per burn hour next to the price on candle pages.
insights.source: Main objection and price follow-up, all-time

insights.title: Friends drive a fifth of first orders
insights.body: 61 of 301 heard about the brand from a friend or family member, second only to Instagram. Ad platforms cannot see these sales, so paid channels look stronger than they are.
insights.action: Add a give-a-candle, get-a-candle referral offer to the post-purchase flow.

insights.title: TikTok is picking up this period
insights.body: 15 of 91 new customers this period came from TikTok against about 8% before. It is the only channel growing beyond normal variation.
insights.action: Turn the strongest scent hook into a TikTok-native video and watch next month's share.
insights.source: How they found you, this period against all-time

insights.title: Diffuser buyers worry about price twice as often
insights.body: 12 of 48 diffuser buyers named price against 17 of 138 signature candle buyers. Diffusers are the higher ticket, so value framing matters more there.
insights.action: Add 'lasts up to 90 days' framing to diffuser pages.

insights.title: People come back when the candle burns down, not when emailed
insights.body: 41 of 110 returning buyers came back because their candle burnt down; 3 because of an email. The replenishment moment exists and nothing catches it.
insights.action: Build a burn-down reminder flow at about five weeks.
insights.source: Returning: what brought you back, all-time

moves.title: Burn-down replenishment flow
moves.body: Send a reminder about five weeks after a 200g candle order, with a new-scent suggestion. This is the moment most returning buyers name.
moves.source: Burnt down 41 of 110; new scent 28 of 110

moves.title: Rethink the promo calendar
moves.body: Only 13 of 110 came back for a sale and 3 for an email. Send fewer discount campaigns and more new-scent launches.

shifts_comment: TikTok is the one clear shift this period. Google search is slightly lower, an early signal worth watching next month. Everything else, including the top objection, is in line with all-time.

questions_to_consider: Several written answers mention scent strength. Consider adding 'Not sure how strong the scent would be' as its own objection option next time you review the survey.
method:
Data pulled live from Zigpoll on 1 October 2026: the Post-Purchase New Customers and Post-Purchase Returning Customers surveys. All-time is 1 June to 30 September 2026; this period is 1 to 30 September (Australia/Brisbane). August had almost no answers (the survey was unpublished for 26 days) and is included in all-time as collected.

Every written answer was read (128 for the problem question, 71 for what returning customers love, 64 'Other' answers). Clear 'Other' answers were counted under the matching option. Product lines come from the Shopify line items attached to 280 responses, counted by hand.

This example uses fictional data for a fictional brand. It shows the shape and depth of a finished report only.
